questions.question:
The Pod `app-frontend` in the namespace `production` is in `CrashLoopBackOff`. Its container expects a configuration file at `/etc/app/config.yaml`, which does not exist in the image.

1. Create a ConfigMap `app-config` in `production` with the key `config.yaml` and the content `database_host: postgres.production.svc.cluster.local`
2. Mount it so that the file `/etc/app/config.yaml` exists in the `app-frontend` container (keep the Pod name, image and command)
3. Make sure the Pod is `Running`

Tip: volumes of an existing Pod cannot be edited in place.

verification.description: ConfigMap app-config has key config.yaml with the right content
app-frontend is Running and reads /etc/app/config.yaml

questions.question:
A developer (user `dev-user`) needs to list Pods and Deployments in the namespace `staging`, and nowhere else.

1. Create a Role `pod-deploy-lister` in `staging` that allows `get` and `list` on `pods` and `deployments`
2. Create a RoleBinding `dev-user-binding` that grants it to the user `dev-user`

Verify with `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n staging --as dev-user`.

verification.description: dev-user can list pods and deployments in staging only
Role and RoleBinding use the required names

questions.question:
The node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` needs maintenance. It runs the Deployment `web-tier` (3 replicas) and a standalone Pod `db-local` that keeps important data on the node (`emptyDir`).

1. Prevent any new Pods from being scheduled on `k3d-cluster-agent-1`
2. Move all `web-tier` Pods off `k3d-cluster-agent-1` (they must stay at `3` Ready replicas)
3. The Pod `db-local` must **not** be evicted, deleted or recreated — it must keep running on `k3d-cluster-agent-1`

Note: think about what `kubectl drain` would do to `db-local`.

verification.description: k3d-cluster-agent-1 is unschedulable
web-tier has 3 Ready replicas, none on k3d-cluster-agent-1
db-local is the original Pod, still Running on k3d-cluster-agent-1

questions.question:
The Deployment `db-app` in the namespace `databases` needs shared persistent storage.

1. Create a StorageClass `fast-ssd` with provisioner `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner` (static provisioning)
2. Create a PersistentVolume `db-pv`: `5Gi`, access mode `ReadWriteMany`, StorageClass `fast-ssd`, `hostPath` `/mnt/db-data`
3. Create a PersistentVolumeClaim `db-storage` in `databases`: `5Gi`, `ReadWriteMany`, StorageClass `fast-ssd`
4. Update `db-app` to mount the claim at `/data` (volume name `data`)

verification.description: StorageClass fast-ssd and PV db-pv are correct
PVC db-storage is Bound to db-pv
db-app mounts db-storage at /data and is available

questions.question:
All Pods in the namespace `shop` can currently talk to each other. Implement isolation with three NetworkPolicies:

1. `frontend-policy`: Pods with `tier=frontend` accept ingress on TCP port `80` only (from any source)
2. `backend-policy`: Pods with `tier=backend` accept ingress only from `tier=frontend` Pods on TCP port `3000`
3. `database-policy`: Pods with `tier=database` accept ingress only from `tier=backend` Pods on TCP port `5432`

Test Pods `frontend`, `backend`, `database` and `tester` (no tier label) already exist. All have `wget`.

verification.description: Three policies select the right Pods, sources and ports
Allowed and denied traffic behaves as required

questions.question:
A Helm chart `monitoring` exists locally in `/tmp/exam/helm-charts/monitoring` on `ckad9999`.

Install it as the release `monitoring-stack` in the namespace `monitoring` (create the namespace if needed), overriding these values:

- `replica_count` = `3`
- `storage_size` = `50Gi`
- `persistence.enabled` = `true`

Inspect the chart's `values.yaml` first.

verification.description: Release monitoring-stack is deployed in monitoring with the overrides
Chart resources reflect the values

questions.question:
Container runtime configuration requires node access, which this lab does not provide, so inspect it through the API instead.

Write one line per node to `/tmp/exam/q7/runtimes.txt` on `ckad9999`, in the format:

`<node-name> <container-runtime-version>`

for example `node1 containerd://1.7.0`. Use the values Kubernetes reports for each node.

verification.description: runtimes.txt lists every node with its runtime

questions.question:
There were unexpected reads of ConfigMaps in the namespace `default`. API audit logging requires control-plane access, which this lab does not provide, so investigate with RBAC instead.

1. Find which ServiceAccounts in the namespace `audit-lab` are allowed to `get` ConfigMaps in the namespace `default`. Write their names, one per line, to `/tmp/exam/q8/cm-access.txt` on `ckad9999`
2. Revoke that access for the ServiceAccount `deployer` only, by deleting the binding that grants it. Do not delete the ServiceAccount and do not change the access of any other ServiceAccount

verification.description: cm-access.txt lists exactly the ServiceAccounts with access
deployer lost access; ci and the ServiceAccounts still exist

questions.question:
The Deployment `web-app` in the namespace `production` runs `2` replicas.

Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `web-app-hpa` for it that keeps the average CPU utilization at `70%`, with a minimum of `2` and a maximum of `10` replicas.

verification.description: HPA web-app-hpa targets web-app with 2-10 replicas at 70% CPU

questions.question:
The Service `api` (port `80`) in the namespace `web-api` must be exposed through an Ingress. The TLS Secret `api-tls-cert` already exists.

Create an Ingress `api-ingress` in `web-api` with ingress class `traefik`:

- TLS for host `api.example.com` using the Secret `api-tls-cert`
- Host `api.example.com`, path `/api` (pathType `Prefix`) → `api:80`
- Host `api.example.com`, path `/health` (pathType `Exact`) → `api:80`

verification.description: Ingress has TLS for api.example.com with api-tls-cert
Ingress routes /api (Prefix) and /health (Exact) to api:80

questions.question:
The Pods of the Deployment `report-generator` in the namespace `sched-debug` have been `Pending` for a long time, and `kubectl describe` shows **no scheduling events** at all.

Find out why no scheduler is placing them and fix the Deployment so that both replicas get scheduled by the cluster's default scheduler and run.

(On a kubeadm cluster this is also what you would see if the `kube-scheduler` static Pod were down — check `kubectl get pods -n kube-system` in that case.)

verification.description: Deployment uses the default scheduler
Both replicas are Running

questions.question:
In the namespace `db-cluster`, deploy a StatefulSet `database-cluster`:

- `3` replicas, Pod label `app=database-cluster`
- Container `postgres`, image `postgres:16-alpine`, port `5432`, env `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=example` and `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata`
- A `volumeClaimTemplate` named `db-storage` requesting `10Gi` (`ReadWriteOnce`, default StorageClass), mounted at `/var/lib/postgresql/data`
- A **headless** Service `database-cluster` on port `5432`, so that Pods get stable DNS names such as `database-cluster-0.database-cluster`

verification.description: Headless Service database-cluster on port 5432
StatefulSet spec is correct
3 Pods Ready with bound PVCs and stable DNS

questions.question:
The namespace `test` consumes too many resources. Configure:

1. A ResourceQuota `test-quota` limiting the namespace to `requests.cpu: 4` and `requests.memory: 8Gi` in total
2. A LimitRange `test-limits` for type `Container` with:
   - `min`: CPU `100m`, memory `128Mi`
   - `max`: CPU `1`, memory `1Gi`
   - `defaultRequest`: CPU `100m`, memory `128Mi`; `default` (limit): CPU `500m`, memory `512Mi`

A Pod requesting `2` CPUs and `2Gi` memory must then be rejected (try it with `--dry-run=server`).

verification.description: ResourceQuota test-quota is correct
LimitRange test-limits is correct
A 2 CPU / 2Gi Pod is rejected, a small Pod is accepted

questions.question:
Configure Pod Security Admission for the namespace `restricted` (create it if missing):

1. `enforce` mode at level `restricted`
2. `audit` mode at level `baseline`

Then verify that a Pod with `privileged: true` is denied (e.g. with `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`).

verification.description: Namespace restricted has the PSA labels
A privileged Pod is rejected

questions.question:
Create a Pod `app-with-logger` in the namespace `default`:

- Container `nginx`, image `nginx:1.25`, mounting the volume `log-volume` at `/var/log/nginx`
- Container `logger`, image `busybox:1.36`, mounting `log-volume` at `/logs` and running `tail -F /logs/access.log`
- `log-volume` is an `emptyDir`

Both containers must keep running, and requests to nginx must show up in the logs of `logger`.

verification.description: Pod spec has both containers sharing log-volume
Both containers run and logger shows nginx requests
